🛡️ Security & Compliance
v1.5.1 — Input Sanitization:

Mandatory input sanitization before all sed and heredoc operations
Shell metacharacter stripping on all user input
200-character field length limits
Content-type validation (names, roles, goals)
Quoted heredoc delimiters to prevent variable expansion
Zero unsanitized user input reaches exec. No exceptions.

v1.5.3 — Metadata & Dependency Clarity:

openclaw CLI now declared in required binaries — was previously used but undeclared
Network activity claims clarified: core setup (Steps 1-3) uses only bash and standard Unix tools with zero network activity. Opt-in features (cron jobs, gateway config, channel integrations) may involve network activity through OpenClaw's platform — each is clearly marked with ⚠️ warnings and requires explicit user approval
Scripts documented: all shell scripts in scripts/ are read-only helpers that output reports — they don't modify system files, make network calls, or access data outside ~/workspace/

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-persona-os
Version: 1.5.2

The skill bundle is primarily designed for benign agent management, with a strong emphasis on security and prompt injection defense for the AI agent. However, the `scripts/setup-wizard.sh` file, intended for *manual* user execution, is vulnerable to shell injection. User-provided input is directly embedded into `cat` heredocs without sanitization, allowing arbitrary command execution if a malicious user runs the script and provides crafted input. This is a critical vulnerability, but it is distinct from the agent's primary setup flow (which includes explicit input sanitization instructions in `SKILL.md`) and does not demonstrate malicious intent within the overall package.

llm.summary: The skill largely matches its description (an agent workspace OS) but contains inconsistencies and potentially risky runtime behavior (notably a required 'openclaw' binary despite claims that it's optional and strong instructions to use exec to run many shell tasks), so review and cautious approval are advised.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims the openclaw CLI is required only for optional features, and SKILL.md repeatedly states openclaw commands are opt-in. Yet the registry metadata marks 'openclaw' as a required binary (listed with bash/sed/find/etc.). Requiring an external platform binary as mandatory is inconsistent with the stated scope (core setup should work with standard Unix tools). The skill also includes many helper scripts (setup-wizard.sh, security-audit.sh, config-validator.sh) that imply more than a pure 'instruction-only' template — legitimate for an 'OS' style package, but the openclaw binary requirement is disproportionate unless channel/gateway automation is intended to be core.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tightly constrains file operations to ~/workspace/ and marks cron/gateway/channel changes as opt-in, which is good. However it also instructs the agent to always use the exec tool (never tell the user to run commands) and to run one exec at a time asking for approval via the exec popup. That model depends on the user approving potentially many shell actions; if users habitually click approve without inspection, the agent could execute arbitrary shell scripts from the package (including the large setup-wizard.sh). The instructions demand exact verbatim outputs for menus and strict agent-driven flows — operationally coherent but high-leverage (agent-run shell commands). If the scripts truly confine themselves to ~/workspace and don't call network or privileged system paths, this is within scope; but those guarantees depend on reviewing the scripts' contents (some large scripts are present but not fully shown).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install spec (no downloads), which reduces supply-chain risk. The repository contains many scripts and templates; these are delivered with the skill (so files will be available for the agent to exec). No network-based installers or remote downloads were observed in the provided manifest. Risk mainly comes from executing included shell scripts — review their contents before approving exec runs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials (good). The only oddity is marking 'openclaw' as a required binary even though SKILL.md says openclaw is only needed for optional features (cron/gateway). The skill references gateway/channel integrations and notes they will require separate credentials when the user opts in — that is proportional. No unrelated credentials are requested in metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (not force-included) and default autonomous invocation are normal. The skill can create files under ~/workspace/ (declared stateDirs) — expected for a workspace OS. The opt-in features include creating cron jobs via openclaw cron add and applying gateway config via openclaw gateway restart; those actions can change the agent's operational environment (scheduling and channel configs) and are privileged when performed, but they are documented as requiring explicit user approval. No evidence the skill modifies other skills or system-wide agent settings beyond its workspace, but the gateway operation would affect channel behavior (network activity via the OpenClaw platform) if enabled.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege
